payload.rationale: I estimate a 16% chance that the final qualifying Weather Company maximum for Los Angeles (CLILAX) on September 18 is 74–75°F, inclusive. No observations or forecasts were supplied, so this is a climatology-based judgment rather than a current-weather forecast. General background knowledge places coastal Los Angeles airport highs commonly in the 70s in September, making this interval plausible, but it covers only two reported degrees. Marine influence and occasional hot offshore conditions produce substantial variation. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that warmer September conditions could put the day's maximum above 75°F. The strongest reason it could be too low is that a persistent marine pattern could concentrate temperatures near 74–75°F more tightly than this broad baseline assumes. Settlement depends on the contract-defined final value, not an approximate reading or downtown Los Angeles temperature.
limitations: No current forecasts, airport observations, or weather-pattern evidence were supplied as of the information cutoff.
No station-specific historical temperature distribution was supplied; the numerical estimate uses approximate general climatological knowledge.
Final Weather Company reporting, rounding, conversion, and revisions can affect settlement near the interval boundaries.
